answer: Distinct interaction history audit.** Each agent identity accrues a private log of pairwise interactions, and a new identity must present a fresh log whose counterparties are disjoint from any existing identity's. Collusion across duplicates collapses when shared counterparties surface as a jade marker in the audit, flagging both. The cost is maintaining a genuine garden of independent partners per identity; cloning forces a whole separate interaction inlet per duplicate, making each copy as expensive as the original.
